sentences.text: Fruitadens is a member of the heterodontosaurid family, a group within the ornithischian dinosaur class.
Its name translates to "Fruita teeth," honoring the Colorado town where the remains were unearthed.
This species holds the record for the smallest ornithischian dinosaur found in North America.
The front of its upper jaw featured a small peg-like tooth situated just before the canine.
Unlike most ornithischians, the leg bones of this animal were hollow, resembling the structure seen in small theropods.
Fossils revealed the presence of replacement teeth in the jaws, a trait rare among its relatives.
Remains belonging to at least four individuals of varying ages were discovered in sandstone beds within the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation.
The genus was formally described in 2009 by Richard Butler and colleagues, though the name was officially published in 2010.
Scientists believe this creature moved on two legs and likely fed on a variety of foods.
Its jaw structure was less specialized than that of earlier relatives, suggesting it acted as a generalist feeder that selected specific plants and invertebrates.
Initially, fossils attributed to this genus were thought to be similar to the Early Cretaceous fabrosaurid Echinodon, but later analysis placed it closer to Heterodontosaurus.
This dinosaur lived during the Tithonian stage, spanning from 149.2 to 143.1 million years ago.

The sites where it lived preserved a diverse community including snails, clams, crabs, insects, lungfish, ray-finned fishes, turtles, rincophidian reptiles, lizards, a mesosuchian crocodylomorph, and early mammals.
